name: Andorra
system_note: A co-principality whose co-princes are the French president and a Spanish bishop.
snapshot: A Pyrenean microstate with two princes, France's president and the Bishop of Urgell, that is negotiating closer ties with the EU while managing a housing squeeze.
culture: Andorra is the only country where Catalan is the sole official language. Romanesque churches dot its valleys, and its co-princes reflect a feudal arrangement dating to 1278. Skiing, hiking and duty-free shopping draw millions of visitors a year, many times the resident population.
society: Low taxes have attracted wealthy residents, including YouTubers and athletes, pushing up housing costs and prompting limits on foreign investment. Most residents are not Andorran citizens; Spaniards and Portuguese are the largest groups. An EU association agreement has been negotiated but faces a referendum.
situation: Xavier Espot Zamora of the Democrats for Andorra has led the government since 2019. In 2026 an association agreement giving Andorra deeper access to the EU single market moved through its final EU approvals; under Andorran law it needs a binding referendum and a two-thirds vote in parliament before ratification. The next general election is due in 2027.
power: A parliamentary co-principality. The head of government is elected by the 28-seat General Council; the two co-princes, the French president and the Bishop of Urgell, are largely ceremonial.

leaders.state: Co-princes Emmanuel Macron and Bishop Josep-Lluís Serrano Pentinat
leaders.gov: Head of Government Xavier Espot Zamora, since 2019
